topic: Underfitting vs Overfitting & The Bias-Variance Tradeoff
headline: This is the #1 concept that trips up 80% of ML beginners.
caption:
Most ML beginners can recite the textbook definition of bias and variance. But ask them how to diagnose them in a real training log, or how to fix them in their pipelines, and they struggle.

The Bias-Variance Tradeoff is the single most important concept to master if you want to build models that actually generalize to unseen data.

In today's carousel, I break down:
1️⃣ Underfitting (High Bias) vs Overfitting (High Variance) with concrete visual analogies.
2️⃣ The Sweet Spot of model complexity.
3️⃣ 3 professional ways to detect model errors.
4️⃣ A concrete engineer's playbook of fixes to tune your models.

What is your go-to technique to fight overfitting in your models? Drop it in the comments below! 👇
